account: Dermatologists at Asan Medical Center, Ulsan University College of Medicine, in Seoul, South Korea, ran a single-center unmasked randomized trial of the Model Dermatology algorithm, a convolutional neural network that the dermatologist Seung Seog Han develops and maintains as a web service. Consecutive adults with one or more skin lesions suspicious for skin cancer were randomly allocated to four non-dermatology trainees and four dermatology residents, who examined them with or without real-time help from the algorithm. Among 576 patients with Fitzpatrick skin types III or IV, the physicians' diagnoses were correct in 53.9% of the 295 cases with help and in 43.8% of the 281 cases without (P = 0.019). The gain came from the non-dermatology trainees, whose accuracy was 54.7% with the algorithm and 30.7% without; for the dermatology residents it was not significant. Han is the first author of the trial report.
